Could someone explain what is happening in american politics right now?

Ok, from the bottom up. Obama is a democrat. The constitution prohibits him from being reelected since he's served two full, four year terms. There is a strong suspicion that he's pushing Vice President Biden to run, though, which would effectively be a continuation of the current policies, just under a different head of state. Sort of like an understudy taking over the lead role of a play.

As for the presidential election, it might help to think of it as two separate elections. First, there are the primaries. That's the phase we're in now. People who want to run declare their candidacy in their preferred party. The primaries are spaced out over several months, it's not all done at once like the actual election is. Primaries are more of a popularity contest than anything else. The democrats' main primary candidates are Hillary Clinton (former US Secretary of State, former US Senator from New York, wife of President Bill Clinton), and Senator Bernie Sanders (US Senator from Vermont, though as an independent). There are a couple of other names, but they don't get much news coverage, if any. The republicans have just about everyone else you see in the news.

Everyone's trying to win their respective party's nomination to run. As the primaries wear on, those who have no chance in hell of winning their respective nominations will bow out until there is a clear winner. The parties then have a convention, officially nominate their candidate to run, and then the parties put all of their time, money, and effort behind that selected candidate. So for now, you have groups of people from the same party all clamoring to climb to the top of the heap in the expectation that everyone else will fall into line if they win. That's why it's a clusterfuck right now.

Once the primaries are done, then the real campaigning will start. There will be a republican and a democrat (and many third party candidates who, all combined, will net less than one percent of all votes cast) running against each other. When it's down to those two people, that's when the really nasty smear campaigns usually start. While the presidential election is going on, every seat in the US House of Representatives will be up for election (they are up every two years), as well as one third of all US Senate seats (a different third is up for election every two years, as well). Neither of these have any bearing on the Presidential election, however, as the US government is not parliamentary like the UK. The executive and legislative branches are separate from each other.

The US President appoints a cabinet (Secretaries of State, Defense, Justice, etc.) to run the executive branch. He also nominates judges to fill vacancies on federal courts. The Senate can reject them, but they cannot just appoint someone themselves.

The republicans are traditionally the more conservative party while the democrats are traditionally more liberal. Both tend to be nanny-state advocates, but in different aspects.

For one thing, there are too many candidates looking for a way to win the presidency. Their focus is on doing whatever it takes to win and avoiding whatever they must to knock them out.

Of course, none of them has a viable plan as to what they will do should they actually succeed. So, once they get there, nothing will really change. High paid lobbyists will continue to run the show no matter who is elected president.

Bernie and the Donald have alot of appeal to voters because they are candid. They call it like they see it. But my feeling is that they are going out on a limb because they know themselves that they are not going to be elected.

Bernie knows that elections are bought and he doesn't have the financial support to buy the presidency, so he is free to be as blunt and critical as he cares to be. He really has nothing to lose.

The Donald also has nothing to lose. He has everything he wants in life, and so winning the presidency would just be a goof for him. What will stop him will be the strength of the GOP establishment and the rabid hatred the media has for him. Even if he goes third party, the voter pool will be diluted and will probably hand the election to the Democratic nominee.

What the Obama presidency has shown is the limits of the power of the presidency to help middle class voters. Obama has served two four year terms. He is prohibited from running again by law.
